subject: HelioSys POC: success metrics, test harness, and milestone owners
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Varma <asha@heliosys.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: HelioSys POC: success metrics, test harness, and milestone owners

Hi Asha —

Great to meet today. Thanks for walking us through the HelioSys call-routing and knowledge-base use case. As promised, here’s a concise post-call recap and proposed POC plan so we’re aligned on success criteria and next steps. Please confirm or flag any items that need to change.

Summary of objectives
- Goal: Replace current API-based answer service for support triage with a Redwood-powered LLM inference path for short-answer responses + reranking.
- Primary success metrics: latency (p95), throughput (requests/sec), unit cost (cost/token), and answer quality (human rating + automated eval).

Proposed POC success criteria (draft)
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation <= 250 ms for 1–2 turn queries (target 200 ms)
- Throughput: sustained 40 requests/sec at 50% concurrency (target 60 req/s peak)
- Cost: amortized cost <= $0.0008 / token (model + infra) under realistic workload
- Quality: custom evaluation harness (50 golden queries) >= 4.2/5 average human rating; auto-eval F1 >= 0.72 for slot extraction tasks

Test harness and instrumentation
- We'll run a comparative test harness with your staging traffic replay for 48 hours.
- Metrics collected: token counts, model variant, batch size, latency histogram, KV cache hit rate, and per-request cost.
- Deliverables: heliosys-poc-success-metrics.xlsx (metric definitions + targets) and heliosys-test-harness-spec.md attached.

Ownership & timeline (proposal)
- Kickoff: week of Jun 22 (prep week Jun 15) — Redwood owner: Mina; HelioSys owner: Asha
- Integration & workload replay: Jun 22–Jun 26 — Redwood infra lead: Rishi; HelioSys infra: Tom
- Evaluation run: Jun 29–Jul 1 (48h steady-state) — measurement and initial analysis by Jul 3
- Readout + next steps: Jul 6

Immediate asks (next steps)
1) Asha: confirm the 48h staging replay access and a sample of 5000 anonymized queries by Jun 18.
2) HelioSys: nominate a single infra contact who can approve network access and accept our test certs (Tom? confirm).
3) Redwood: Rishi will prepare a baseline config and estimated cost envelope by Jun 16.

Attachments: heliosys-poc-success-metrics.xlsx (metric definitions), heliosys-test-harness-spec.md (replay and eval plan)

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

— Mina Haddad
Mina Haddad | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Asha Varma <asha@heliosys.com>

Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelioSys POC: success metrics, test harness, and milestone owners

Mina —

Thanks for the clear recap. That all looks sensible. A couple of clarifications from our side before we lock dates:

1) For latency, is the 250 ms p95 target measured at the application edge (after our proxy) or just model inference time? We need to know whether to include our network hop in the SLA.
2) For the quality rubric, can you include an example scoring sheet so our CS team can align on the human-rating scale?

We can provide the 5k anonymized queries by Jun 18. Tom will be the infra contact for certificate approvals and staging access; he’s CC’d.

Can you share the baseline cost envelope you mentioned and confirm whether you’ll test with a quantized variant vs fp16? We have licensing constraints around commercial models; happy to discuss model family choices in the kickoff.

Best,
Asha
Asha Varma | Director, Product — HelioSys
asha@heliosys.com | +1 (617) 555-0202

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelioSys POC: success metrics, test harness, and milestone owners

Mina / team —

Thanks — I sketched a technical plan and an internal checklist for the POC. High level thoughts below (will populate the spreadsheet with numbers):

Measurement framing
- We should measure both model-only inference time (server-side) and end-to-end from HelioSys proxy to response. That will let us separate networking from model performance. Report both p50/p95/p99.

Model & perf plan
- Baseline model: open-family 7B fp16 variant (low-latency kernels)
- Cost-optimized variant: 7B int8 quantized (expected token-cost reduction ~30–40%)
- Start with batch_size=1 latency path; enable continuous batching only for throughput runs.

Expected cost envelope (ballpark; will refine in spreadsheet)
- fp16 baseline: approx $0.0014 / token (including infra) under light-load; with batching and KV caching we expect $0.0009–0.0011 / token at scale
- int8 quantized: target <= $0.0008 / token with caching + batching tuned

Success gating logic
- Gate A (must): end-to-end p95 <= 350 ms OR model-only p95 <= 220 ms (we can tolerate 130–150ms of network hop for your proxy)
- Gate B (nice-to-have): cost <= $0.0008/token AND quality >= 4.2/5 on human rating; otherwise recommend 2-week follow-up optimization window

Runbook highlights
- Pre-kickoff checklist: access (staging replay bucket), test certs, baseline telemetry hooks (trace IDs), and agreed golden queries set.
- During run: ramp traffic to target QPS, collect tokens-per-request, KV hit rates, latency histograms, and model variant mapping.
- Post-run: automated evaluation script + manual human label set (20 random samples per reviewer).

Owners (internal)
- Infra & perf config: Rishi Malhotra
- Evaluation & human-ratings: Laura Bennett
- Customer project manager / comms: Mina Haddad
- Engineering assist (integration): Dev Patel

I’ll post concrete numbers to the attachment by EOD Tue (Jun 16). If HelioSys is fine with testing both fp16 and int8, that gives us a clear path to hit the cost target.

— Rishi

Team —

Thanks Rishi — this is the right level of detail. Quick internal checklist before kickoff:
- Rishi: finalize the spreadsheet with estimated token cost ranges and two run configs (fp16 baseline, int8 optimized) by EOD today.
- Dev: confirm the test cert and pre-signed staging bucket access flow; coordinate with Tom for cert pinning.
- Laura: prepare the human-rating rubric and a one-pager for HelioSys CS by Jun 18. Include the 1–5 scale anchor definitions and two sample scored queries.
- Mina: schedule the Jun 22 kickoff (30m) and include a 15m tech sync on Jun 23 for engineering-specific items.

Asha / Tom — please confirm Tom as infra approver and the June 18 sample data delivery. If we get the sample and certs on time we’ll be green to run the Jun 29–Jul 1 evaluation window as proposed.

I’ll attach the updated spreadsheet once Rishi posts it.

— Mina
